title: Public demo report PDFs ship without the canon-mandated synthetic-data marker while carrying production GDPR/confidential boilerplate
evidence: Design artifact (in-chunk): "Every AI report carries the standard disclaimer; the report footer notes 'Synthetic demo data — not a real applicant.'" pdftotext of report-a-aoife.pdf: "This document contains personal data. Retain only for the duration of your tenancy decision and dispose of securely thereafter. Do not share, forward, or reproduce without authorisation." and "Confidential · Personal data (GDPR)". Verification: `for f in server/priv/static/demo/*.pdf; do pdftotext "$f" - | grep -icE "synthetic|not a real applicant|demo"; done` → 0 for all 8 files.
detail: 8 ungated, immutable static assets assert they contain real GDPR personal data yet never mark the data as synthetic, despite the approved design requiring the footer note. No real PII today, but the public asset is mislabeled and the marker is absent.
recommended_fix: Add a 'Synthetic demo data — not a real applicant' footer to the PDFs via the pre-bake pipeline (audit_report template or pdf_prebake overlay) and regenerate all 8 assets.

title: Demo report download URL never matches a shipped PDF — every demo download 404s
evidence: demo_store.gleam:197 analysis id: `"an-aoife",`. demo_api.gleam:521 `let application_id = string.drop_start(analysis_id, 3)`; :528 `let url = "/static/demo/report-" <> application_id <> ".pdf"`. Shipped assets are report-a-aoife.pdf, report-a-conor.pdf, ... (worktree ls). drop_start("an-aoife", 3) = "aoife" (gleam_stdlib: "assert drop_start(from: \"The Lone Gunmen\", up_to: 2) == \"e Lone Gunmen\""), so the URL is /static/demo/report-aoife.pdf — no such file; the code's own comment claims the mapping yields "a-aoife".
detail: The demo's only sanctioned network call fetches a URL that never resolves; download mock report (acceptance item and the felt-value CTA moment) fails with an internal-error toast. Functional, not an injection/SSRF issue: same-origin static GET, id derived from fixtures.
recommended_fix: Map analysis id to the baked file correctly (e.g. strip the "an-" prefix to "a-aoife", or key report_filenames()/URLs off the analysis id) and add a URL assertion to a test.

title: CI no-network lint is a grep over import strings — JS FFI and file-scoped exceptions bypass it; the promised fetch-spy test is not shipped
evidence: test.yml:132 `VIOLATIONS=$(grep -rn "rsvp\|api_helpers" client/src/demo/ --include="*.gleam" || true)`; :136 `FETCH_VIOLATIONS=$(grep -rln "gleam/fetch" client/src/demo/ --include="*.gleam" | grep -v "demo_api.gleam" || true)`. demo_analytics.gleam:16 `@external(javascript, "./demo_analytics_ffi.mjs", "capture")` — .mjs files are never scanned. demo_flow_test.gleam header: "with zero network involved (the demo effects are synchronous dispatches; the CI demo-no-network grep lint bans rsvp / fetch / api_helpers imports in demo/ as the structural guard)" — no fetch spy exists.
detail: The lint is not a no-op (verified: zero violations on the reviewed tree) but it is heuristic: a future demo module could reach the network via an @external JS FFI or new network code inside demo_api.gleam without tripping it. No live bypass exists today — the only demo .mjs performs no fetch.
recommended_fix: Extend the lint to scan client/src/demo/*.mjs for fetch/XMLHttpRequest, or add a runtime test stubbing window.fetch and asserting the demo walkthrough issues zero requests (the design's original fetch-spy claim).
